pr_title: simplify get_class_in_module and fix for paths containing a dot
pr_body:
# What does this PR do?

A simpler implementation of get_class_in_module that also works when the path starts with e.g. `./` or otherwise contains dot characters *outside* of the repo ID.

Fixes #29251

I should write a test. The test in #29175 didn't fail before the PR (with code from commit 89c64817c), so it does not seem valid.

This does change the API of get_class_in_module to expect the path to an actual file, with the extension - but since the previous PR changed the API already, this seems fine.

comments:
@cebtenzzre could you try updating your library from the main branch and try again 
```
pip install -U git+https://github.com/huggingface/transformers
```
also your command should be updated into this
```
python -c 'from transformers import AutoModel; AutoModel.from_pretrained("./", trust_remote_code=True)'
```
there is a wide difference between `.` and  `./`

i have also tried it with older version of the transformers (`4.37.2`)  library and it works well 
the only problem is that you need to use 
```python
AutoModel.from_pretrained("./", trust_remote_code=True) # works
AutoModel.from_pretrained(".", trust_remote_code=True) # will create an error
```

![image](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/assets/70411813/ec363e5d-d552-464e-8feb-30d407a933bf)

I am already on the latest commit (c8d98405a8f7b0e5d07391b671dcc61bb9d7bad5).

`AutoModel.from_pretrained('.')` works as I would expect for models that do not require trust_remote_code - it loads the model from the current directory. If this is only by accident, maybe transformers should throw an exception if `'.'` is ever passed as the model path, so that developers like me don't start to rely on this fact and then have it fail with a cryptic error in edge cases like this.
This is also a bug in our repo handling, and likely has the same cause that we fixed in #29175. It's on my list to fix - hopefully we can make it work with small tweaks to that PR.

@Rocketknight1 i don't think it's related to #29175 tbh, but let's monkey-patch this one too with 
```python
# or generalise it by using startswith taking into consideration this usecase too 
# AutoModel.from_pretrained(".myfolder", trust_remote_code=True) # it starts with a dot . 
if repo_id == "." :  
   repo_id = "./"
```
pretty sure this is the last problem for imports, didn't encounter anything with your patch tbh, it's stable to all the stress tests i've done so far, so i'll let you handle this one.

I'm not sure why `importlib.machinery.SourceFileLoader` isn't used in all cases - `module_path = module_path.replace(os.path.sep, ".")` without *at least* a prior `assert "." not in module_path` seems like a bad idea, period. What if module_path contains `/./`, or `/../`?

And replacing the "." with "/" just to try and replace it back with "." doesn't make a lot of sense either.

review_comments: module_path now expects the file extension too now. Maybe that should be reflected here too? @cebtenzzre

could you return the original parameter `repo_id` also the documentation for it too, changing parameter names or removing them should not be be done this fast, usually the maintainers deperacate a parameter after a big release of the library in case other libraries or modules use this function too, so it's too much effort.
